title: Premium candidate research, 2026-10-07
note: Condensed from the manual Premium candidate decision report. It is a reference, not a ranking. Atlas Auto uses it as context for the Research Agent and as a labelled fallback when the agents are unavailable. Scores were set by that report; workflow_quality was added for Atlas Auto. Google Ads Performance Coach led that report, but nothing here selects a winner.

candidates.name: Google Ads Performance Coach
candidates.persona: An owner, marketer, or consultant who already runs Google Ads and can export reports, but does not know which number to trust before changing a budget.
candidates.problem: Ad spend decisions are made on conversion numbers that may not measure a qualified outcome. A generic chatbot will happily optimize the wrong conversion.
workflow: Define what counts as a qualified outcome for the business.
Export current and previous Google Ads campaign reports, GA4 traffic and landing-page reports, and a conversion-actions screenshot.
Run the measurement check first. If the primary conversion is not a qualified outcome, stop and report that.
Calculate totals and period-over-period changes in a workbook whose formulas stay visible.
Label each point as a confirmed finding, a possible explanation, or a recommendation.
The owner verifies the evidence and decides whether to change anything in Google Ads. The Blueprint never edits the account.
candidates.before: The owner compares two dashboards by hand, trusts the conversion count, and moves budget on a hunch.
candidates.after: The owner knows whether the numbers can be trusted, sees calculated changes with visible formulas, and gets a short evidence-labelled list of what to verify next.
candidates.why_pay: Bad conversion tracking makes every other optimization wrong. Catching one bad setup on an account spending hundreds or thousands a month justifies the kit.
major_risks: Stating savings or ROI the exports do not support.
A user changing live bids from a hypothesis.
Report layouts change and break the workbook rules.
Useless to businesses that do not advertise.
candidates.estimated_premium_value: Low hundreds as a one-time kit, or about $49-$149/month later, anchored to monthly ad spend. Value estimate, not a price.
candidates.sample_output:
MEASUREMENT REVIEW FIRST
Confirmed: Spring Promo's primary conversion is page_view, not a qualified lead.
Confirmed: /spring-landing receives 85% of paid sessions.
Interpretation: Spring Promo's cost per conversion ($19.38) is not meaningful until tracking changes.
Recommendation (you decide): Set form_submit as primary for Spring Promo, then re-run in 14 days. Do not change bids yet.
candidates.guided_demo: A fictional account where a page view is the primary conversion. The demo stops at 'measurement review first', then shows one confirmed finding and one hypothesis, and states that the numbers are invented.
candidates.novelty_note: Existing playbook material at app/playbooks/google-ads-audit is a manual audit, not a signed-in Premium kit.
candidates.score_summary: Strong teaching point (check measurement before efficiency) with export-only permissions. Narrow: only for businesses already advertising.

candidates.name: AI Collections Assistant
candidates.persona: A service business or clinic with net-30 invoices and roughly $10k or more sitting in accounts receivable.
candidates.problem: Cash is earned but not collected. Owners avoid the awkward follow-up and chase invoices in no particular order.
workflow: Export the overdue-invoice aging report from QuickBooks, Xero, or a CSV.
Skip disputed invoices and credit memos using explicit rules.
Build a priority queue by amount, age, and customer history.
Draft a follow-up per invoice in the owner's voice, escalating tone by age.
The owner reviews and sends each draft. Nothing is sent automatically.
candidates.before: The owner scrolls an aging report once a month and writes a few awkward emails to whoever comes to mind.
candidates.after: A weekly queue chases the largest, oldest, cleanest invoices first with ready-to-review drafts.
candidates.why_pay: One collected invoice covers the cost. The queue, escalation rules, and dispute check are what a single chatbot prompt does not give you.
candidates.estimated_premium_value: About $29-$79/month equivalent, anchored to one recovered invoice. Value estimate, not a price.
candidates.sample_input:
invoice,customer,amount,days_overdue,status
INV-1042,Harbor Dental,$4,200,47,open
INV-1051,Lopez Landscaping,$860,12,open
INV-1038,Brightline Co,$2,150,63,disputed
candidates.sample_output:
QUEUE (skipped 1 disputed)
1. INV-1042 Harbor Dental, $4,200, 47 days. Confirmed: no payment recorded. Draft: firm second reminder.
2. INV-1051 Lopez Landscaping, $860, 12 days. Draft: friendly nudge.
Skipped: INV-1038 (disputed; needs your call).
You review and send each draft.
candidates.guided_demo: A fictional aging report of 8 invoices becomes a ranked queue with one disputed invoice skipped and two drafts at different tones.
candidates.novelty_note: Turns a published use case into a weekly operating ritual with explicit skip and escalation rules.
candidates.score_summary: Broad, frequent, and tied directly to cash. Easier for a generic chatbot to imitate than the ads workflow.

candidates.name: Quote Request Assistant
candidates.persona: A contractor, home-service business, agency, or custom shop getting about 5-30 quote requests a week.
candidates.problem: Quote requests arrive in inconsistent formats. Staff spend 20-30 minutes per request reconstructing scope before pricing anything.
workflow: Paste or forward a quote request.
Extract structured scope, timeline, location, and budget signals.
Judge fit against the owner's written qualification rules.
List clarifying questions and draft an acknowledgment.
Add a tracker row. The owner prices and sends.
candidates.before: Requests sit in an inbox until someone has time to read them carefully, and some are lost.
candidates.after: Every request has a structured scope, a fit judgment with reasons, and a draft reply within the hour.
candidates.why_pay: The expensive part is reconstructing scope, not writing a polite reply. Faster, consistent qualification wins jobs.
major_risks: Leaking internal pricing notes into a draft.
candidates.estimated_premium_value: About $39-$99/month equivalent when slow quotes mean lost jobs. Value estimate, not a price.
candidates.sample_input: From website form: 'Need our back deck redone, maybe 300 sq ft, composite if not crazy expensive. Hoping before July. We're in Riverside.'
candidates.sample_output:
Confirmed: deck replacement, ~300 sq ft, Riverside, wants completion before July.
Interpretation: budget-sensitive ("if not crazy expensive").
Fit: YES (in service area, above minimum size).
Questions: existing structure condition? railing included?
You price and send.
candidates.guided_demo: One fictional request flows through extraction, fit rules, and clarifying questions into a tracker row.
candidates.novelty_note: Adds owner-written qualification rules and a tracker to an otherwise summarization-style task.
candidates.score_summary: Close to revenue and easy to demonstrate. Collapses into 'summarize this email' if the rules are thin.

candidates.name: AI Expense Watchdog
candidates.persona: An owner who has not looked line by line at software and vendor spend for months.
candidates.problem: Forgotten subscriptions, duplicate tools, and quiet price increases accumulate in card and bank statements.
workflow: Export a few months of card, bank, or accounting transactions as CSV.
Group recurring charges by vendor and cadence.
Flag price increases and possible duplicate tools.
Produce a short review list with only the savings the data supports.
The owner decides what to cancel. Nothing is cancelled for them.
candidates.before: Recurring charges blur together and nobody owns the review.
candidates.after: A monthly ledger of recurring charges with flagged increases and duplicates to review.
candidates.why_pay: Forgotten subscriptions are concrete money. The product is the repeatable monthly check, not a summary of a statement.
major_risks: False 'you could save this much' claims.
Cancelling a tool the business still needs.
Sensitive financial data in an AI tool.
candidates.estimated_premium_value: About $19-$49/month equivalent, only if the first run finds something. Value estimate, not a price.
candidates.sample_output:
Confirmed: DesignHub Pro rose from $29 to $39 (+$10/month) in August.
Interpretation: DesignHub Pro and CanvaLite Teams may overlap (both design tools).
Review: confirm who uses each before cancelling either.
candidates.guided_demo: Three months of fictional card transactions become a recurring-charge ledger with one increase and one possible duplicate.
candidates.novelty_note: CSV-first instead of the published record's bank aggregation.
candidates.score_summary: Applies to almost every SMB and is read-only. Dollar value is often small and one-time.

candidates.name: No-show Recovery Assistant
candidates.persona: A clinic, salon, fitness studio, or consultant with several no-shows a month.
candidates.problem: Missed appointments are lost revenue the same day, and the rebooking message usually never gets sent.
workflow: Export the day's booking list with attendance status and open slots.
Confirm the no-show against the booking record.
Draft one rebooking message with real open times and the client's contact preference.
Flag repeat no-shows for a human policy decision.
The owner reviews and sends. Consent is checked before any message.
candidates.before: Staff mean to follow up on no-shows but rarely do, and slots stay empty.
candidates.after: Each missed visit gets a timely, specific rebooking draft with real open times.
candidates.why_pay: An empty slot is lost revenue the same day, and the upgrade from template to triggered draft is real.
major_risks: Offering a slot that is not open.
candidates.estimated_premium_value: About $49-$99/month equivalent for a busy appointment book. Value estimate, not a price.
candidates.sample_input:
time,client,service,status,contact_pref,sms_consent
10:00,J. Rivera,Cut & color,no_show,sms,yes
11:30,A. Chen,Consult,attended,email,no
Open: Thu 2:00, Fri 9:30
candidates.sample_output:
Confirmed: J. Rivera missed 10:00 Cut & color; SMS consent on file.
Draft (SMS): 'Hi J., we missed you today. Would Thu 2:00 or Fri 9:30 work instead?'
You review and send.
candidates.guided_demo: A fictional day's bookings with one no-show produce one rebooking draft with real open slots and a consent check.
candidates.novelty_note: Draft-only premium version avoids the published record's automatic SMS.
candidates.score_summary: Obvious money story, but fragmented booking systems and SMS consent make setup and permissions hard.
